claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

## Summary

**You are NOT eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

**The key reason:** Another person who lives with Alex has priority for the Child Benefit claim. Under UK rules, only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child. When two people are responsible for the same child, they need to agree who will claim, or HMRC will decide. Since another claimant living with Alex has already been determined to have priority, you cannot make a successful claim.

**Other factors in your situation:**
- ✓ Alex is 19 and in approved education (normally eligible - children under 20 in approved education qualify)
- ✓ Alex working 24+ hours/week doesn't disqualify them since they're still in approved education
- ✓ Alex being in hospital for 11 weeks is under the 12-week limit
- ✗ **The other claimant's priority is the deciding factor**

If circumstances change and the other person stops claiming, or if you want to discuss changing who receives the benefit, you would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss your options.

reasonings: Alex is 19 years old and in approved education, which would normally make them eligible for Child Benefit (as children under 20 in approved education qualify). However, there is a critical factor that makes you ineligible: another claimant who lives with the child has priority. According to the rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child, and if you and someone else are both responsible for the same child, you need to agree who will claim, or HMRC will decide. Since another claimant living with Alex has priority, you cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex. The other factors in Alex's situation do not override this fundamental rule: (1) The fact that Alex works 24+ hours/week would normally disqualify them, BUT they are still in approved education which is an exception - the rules state you stop getting Child Benefit if your child 'starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week AND is no longer in approved education or training', so working while in education doesn't disqualify them; (2) Alex being in hospital for 11 weeks is under the 12-week threshold after which Child Benefit would normally stop; (3) Alex not receiving qualifying benefits in their own right means this doesn't disqualify them. However, the decisive factor remains that another claimant with whom Alex lives has priority, making you ineligible to claim.
